title: Steve Owens: Heisman Winner, Norman Businessman and OU AD
question: Was Heisman winner Steve Owens ever OU's athletic director?
answer: Steve Owens, OU's 1969 Heisman winner, served as the university's athletic director from August 1996 to March 1998 after building several businesses in Norman.
summary: 1969 Heisman winner Steve Owens (OU 1967-69) built businesses in Norman, helped found the Oklahoma Sports Hall of Fame and served as OU athletic director.
body: Steve Owens graduated from Miami High School in northeast Oklahoma and attended OU from 1966 through 1969, earning All-Big Eight honors in 1967, 1968 and 1969. He was a workhorse in every sense. Owens set Sooner records for career rushing touchdowns (56), carries in a season (358) and carries in a single game (55, against Oklahoma State), and he won the Heisman Trophy in 1969.
The Detroit Lions picked him 19th overall in the 1970 draft. He was named All-Pro in 1971 and 1972 before a knee injury ended his playing career after five seasons.

Owens then came home and went to work. According to the Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History and Culture, he ran several Norman-based companies, including Steve Owens and Associates, FORESIGHT, Inc. and Owens-Powell and Associates, and stayed active with a long list of charities.

He also helped build the state's sports history infrastructure. Owens was a founder of the Oklahoma Sports Hall of Fame, which later merged with the Jim Thorpe Athletic Club to form the Jim Thorpe Association. He entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1991 and was the Walter Camp Foundation's Alumnus of the Year that same year.

In August 1996, OU turned to its old Heisman winner to lead the athletic department, and Owens served as athletic director until March 1998. Few people have touched the Sooner program from as many angles: record-setting back, booster, businessman and administrator.
